correctness.rationale: Exact Chebyshev scalar two-cycle and Fourier spectrum identify unique simple +1 checkerboard mode at a*. Two-colour mean equations are analytically solvable by IFT because their determinant is 1−A0A1≠0; their reduced odd equation dH(a,d²)=0 has Ha=8√6 and Ht=B>0 proved by rational radical bounds, hence exactly two lower-side branches. Lyapunov–Schmidt uniqueness and two-site translation symmetry exclude other nearby full-ring branches. Reduced Schur complement gives unstable multiplier 1+16√6(a*−a)+O((a*−a)²); other modes contract by continuity. NumPy standalone code passes 124 finite checks; analytical proof supports all fixed even N≥4.

value.rationale: The first transverse instability of a physically natural synchronized coupled-map two-cycle occurs in a forced alternating Fourier mode. Computing the nonlinear pitchfork sign determines whether symmetry-breaking cycles can be stable/unstable and whether they coexist with the synchronized attractor. The theorem supplies an exact subcritical two-saddle local branch count and sharp amplitude and multiplier coefficients for every fixed even ring, information absent from linear Floquet stability windows. It is a structural local classification, not an arbitrary numerical parameter slice.
